h1: The 7 Best Shark Robot Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Shark Robot Vacuums: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 7 best Shark robot vacuums of 2026, covering AI Ultra, Matrix Plus mop combos and Navigator budget models.
summary: The Shark AI Ultra AV2511AE is our best overall for its AI home mapping and Matrix Clean navigation. The AV2501S suits pet owners who want a HEPA bagless base, and the SharkMatrix Plus AV2610WA is the 2-in-1 pick for mixed floors. The Navigator AV2120 is the cheapest sensible entry.
intro: Shark's robot vacuum range is confusing because the names barely tell you what you are buying. A Navigator, an AI Ultra and a Matrix Plus can look similar on a shelf, yet one empties itself, one mops and one does neither. Many buyers choose on color and price, then discover the dock or mop they wanted was never part of that model.

We reviewed seven Shark models and ranked them on paper by navigation, dock design, mopping and price tier. The list comes from spec sheets and owner reports rather than bench numbers, and each pick is placed by the specific trade it makes against its neighbors in the family.

products.name: Shark AI Ultra Robot Vacuum, AV2511AE
products.verdict: The smartest Shark for navigation and home mapping.
products.description:
The AV2511AE combines AI home mapping with Matrix Clean navigation and is Self-Empty compatible. It is vacuum only and sits in the $200-500 bracket.

It ranks first because navigation is the thing that separates a good robot from a frustrating one, and this is the most capable system in the Shark line here. The AV2501S below it offers a bagless base but relies on simpler mapping.

It suits buyers who want the best Shark brain and do not need mopping. The caveat is that Self-Empty compatible means the base may be a separate purchase, so check the bundle.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want the best Shark navigation and mapping.
products.skipIf: You want mopping built into the robot.

products.name: Shark AV2501S AI Ultra Robot Vacuum with Matrix Clean
products.verdict: A HEPA bagless base built around pet hair.
products.description:
The AV2501S uses Matrix Clean mapping with a bagless HEPA self-empty base with 30 days of capacity, and it targets pet hair.

It ranks second because it brings the dock the AV2511AE lacks in the box, though with less advanced mapping. Bagless also means no bag purchases, at the cost of rinsing a bin.

It suits pet households that want long intervals. The caveat is the 30 day figure is a claim, and it does not mop.
products.idealFor: Pet owners wanting a dock and no bag costs.
products.skipIf: You need wet cleaning on hard floors.

products.name: SharkMatrix Plus 2-in-1 Robot Vacuum & Mop, AV2610WA
products.verdict: One robot for vacuuming and mopping mixed floors.
products.description:
The AV2610WA is a 2-in-1 vacuum and mop with Matrix navigation, a Black and Brass finish, and Self-Empty compatibility, priced in the $200-500 bracket.

It ranks third because mopping adds value that the vacuum-only AI Ultra models skip, though it leaves out the AI mapping. Against the AV2613WA below it, this is the fuller-featured version.

It suits homes with hard floors and carpet. The caveat is that, as with the others, the dock may be sold separately.
products.idealFor: Homes mixing hard floors and carpet.
products.skipIf: You only need vacuuming and want AI mapping.

products.name: Shark Navigator Robot Vacuum + Self-Empty Base, RV2120AE
products.description:
The RV2120AE includes a Self-Empty base, SmartPath navigation and a bagless dock, and it is vacuum only in the $200-500 bracket.

It ranks fourth because it delivers the dock convenience of the AI Ultra line with simpler SmartPath navigation. It beats the dockless Navigators by saving you from emptying after every run.

It suits buyers who want automatic emptying without flagship money. The caveat is that SmartPath is less sophisticated than Matrix mapping.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting a dock without flagship pricing.
products.skipIf: You want advanced mapping or mopping.

products.name: Shark Matrix Plus 2-in-1 Robot Vacuum & Mop, AV2613WA
products.verdict: A lower-cost way into the Matrix Plus mop system.
products.description:
The AV2613WA is another 2-in-1 vacuum and mop with Matrix navigation and a Black and Brass finish, positioned at mid-range pricing.

It ranks fifth because the spec sheet lists fewer details than the AV2610WA, such as no dock note. It exists for buyers who want the mop system for a bit less.

It suits shoppers who want mopping and do not need every extra. The caveat is the thinner listing, so verify bundle contents.
products.idealFor: Shoppers wanting mopping at a lower cost.
products.skipIf: You need a confirmed self-empty dock.

products.name: Shark Matrix Plus Robot Vacuum and Mop, UR2650WS
products.verdict: A compact budget mop combo for hard floor homes.
products.description:
The UR2650WS is a vacuum and mop combo with a compact profile in the budget 2-in-1 tier, focused on hard floors.

It ranks sixth because the hard floor focus narrows its appeal compared with the AV-series Matrix Plus models. Its compact body is its advantage in tight spaces.

It suits apartments with mostly hard floors. The caveat is lighter carpet suitability and fewer listed features.
products.skipIf: You have a lot of carpet.

products.name: Shark Navigator Robot Vacuum, SmartPath Navigation, AV2120
products.verdict: The no-frills Shark for people who just want clean floors.
products.description:
The AV2120 is a compact, white, vacuum-only robot with SmartPath navigation in the $100-200 bracket. It has no mop and no dock.

It ranks last because it lacks the dock of the RV2120AE and the mapping of the AI Ultra line. It is simply the cheapest way into the brand.

It suits small spaces and first robots. The caveat is that you empty the bin yourself and there is no mopping.
products.idealFor: Small spaces and first-time robot owners.
products.skipIf: You want a dock or mop.

whatMatters.detail: Shark uses AI home mapping, Matrix navigation and SmartPath across the range. Mapping systems plan routes and remember rooms, while simpler ones cover floors less efficiently. Check the listing for the exact navigation name before buying.

Self-Empty compatible means the robot works with a base but may not ship with one. A model with the base included will be clearly stated. Read the title and bullets, because the price gap between the two can be large.

Bagless bases like the one on the AV2501S avoid bag purchases but need a bin emptied and rinsed. Bag systems stay cleaner but cost more over time. Choose based on whether you prefer chores or consumables.
2-in-1 models wipe hard floors with a damp pad, saving a separate chore. They add a water tank and are not suited to thick carpet. Only pay for it if hard floors dominate your home.
Shark releases many near-identical model numbers, such as AV2610WA and AV2613WA. Small suffix differences can mean different bundles. Compare the bullet lists, not just the product name.

howToChoose.intro: Floor type decides whether a 2-in-1 mop is useful or wasted money.

cards.label: Vacuum only
cards.text: Better navigation options and simpler design, ideal for carpet and pet hair. Picks here: the AI Ultra AV2511AE, AV2501S and the Navigators.

cards.label: 2-in-1
cards.text: Adds mopping for hard floors but fewer premium navigation options. Picks here: the Matrix Plus AV2610WA, AV2613WA and UR2650WS.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to vacuum only unless hard floors dominate.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A compact body, simple operation and an optional dock so the robot fits tight spaces and a smaller budget.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Shark Navigator AV2120 has a compact design at the lowest price, and the UR2650WS adds mopping in a compact profile for hard floors.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want smart mapping and long hands-off intervals, where the Shark AI Ultra AV2511AE and AV2501S pay off.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You have a small space and tidy floors, where the Navigator AV2120 handles the basics for far less.

faq.q: Does every Shark robot include a self-empty base?
faq.a: No. Some include it, like the RV2120AE, while others are only Self-Empty compatible. Read the product title and bullets before ordering.

faq.q: What is the biggest Shark buying mistake?
faq.a: Assuming a model number tells you the features. Near-identical numbers can differ in dock or mopping. Compare the bullet lists carefully.

faq.q: Is the AI Ultra worth it over a Navigator?
faq.a: If you want better mapping and a smarter route, yes. For a small, simple space, a Navigator is enough. The dock is the other deciding factor.

faq.q: How do I set up a Shark robot?
faq.a: Place the base on a hard floor by a wall, charge the robot and use the app to map your home. Run a first clean with doors open. Then set schedules.
Clear hair from the brush roll, wash or replace filters and empty or rinse the bin as needed. Wipe the sensors regularly. Mop pads on 2-in-1 models need washing.
It vacuums carpet but should not mop it. Look for carpet handling noted on the listing. Where unsure, keep the mop off rugs.

finalTake: The Shark AI Ultra AV2511AE is the best Shark robot vacuum for most buyers because of its smart navigation and mapping. The AV2501S is the pick for pet owners, and the SharkMatrix Plus AV2610WA covers mixed floors with mopping. If you only want something simple and cheap, the Navigator AV2120 is a sensible entry.
